events.did: 在结局前一周（1 WEEK BEFORE THE END）、SEVERAL STATES AWAY 的小木屋旁用斧子劈开木柴并把木柴扔上堆
events.quote_anchor: The wood split and tumbled off the block, and Mitchell Turner tossed the logs onto the growing pile.

events.did: gathered half a dozen logs and set off toward the little red cabin
events.quote_anchor: He gathered half a dozen logs and set off toward the little red cabin.

events.did: called for Syd, dropped the wood onto the rug when she did not answer, and called for Sydney again
events.quote_anchor: When she didn’t answer, the peace he’d felt outside began to falter. He dropped the wood onto the rug.

events.did: told Sydney to keep the decibels down when he is not in the house
events.quote_anchor: “Keep the decibels down when I’m not in the house. If there’s trouble, you need to be able to hear it.”

events.did: said Dol would let her know, and the black shape under the table coalesced into a massive black dog
events.quote_anchor: As if on cue, the shape beneath the table stirred, and straightened, coalescing into a massive black dog.

events.did: blacked out the rest of the library textbook instead of only highlighting the useful passages
events.quote_anchor: Tensed when he saw she wasn’t just highlighting the useful passages. She was blacking out the rest.

events.did: shuffled the pack of playing cards until he found the queen of spades and offered it like an offering
events.quote_anchor: He shuffled until he found a queen of spades and held it like an offering.

events.did: shook her head and refused to go, saying she was good
events.quote_anchor: But this one shook her head, her focus squarely on the book. “I’m good.”

relations.did: 是 Sydney Clarke 的父亲/养父：她用 “Dad” 逗他，他叫她 “boss”
relations.quote_anchor: She rolled her eyes, but her mouth twitched. “Sure, Dad.”

relations.did: 把狗 Dol 从死里带回来，已经 Twice（两次）
relations.quote_anchor: Which might have had something to do with the fact Sydney had brought the dog back from the dead.

relations.did: 与 Victor 是同伴；Syd 打黑字涂书的做法让他想起 Victor 抹掉一首诗
relations.quote_anchor: She was blacking out the rest. Like Victor used to. Only, instead of a poem, all that remained were words like carbon-containing compounds

relations.did: 和 Sydney 一起躲藏；希望她学 coding computers 而不是像他那样跟着他的脚步学医
relations.quote_anchor: Mitch sighed. “Right,” he said, wishing she’d taken an interest in coding computers instead of people. Followed in his footsteps, instead of Victor’s.

numbers.did: 斧子把木头劈开并陷进下面的木墩 half an inch
numbers.quote_anchor: Mitch brought the axe down again, eliciting a crack like a peal of thunder as the blade split the wood and buried itself half an inch in the block beneath.

numbers.did: 小木屋是过去 three years 里收集又抛弃的一系列 lodgings 之一
numbers.quote_anchor: The cabin—it was the latest in a string of lodgings collected and abandoned over the last three years, some lasting months, others only weeks.

numbers.did: 这一处木屋住了 almost a year，足够看完四季变换
numbers.quote_anchor: This one had held for almost a year. Long enough to watch the seasons change, the woods behind the house going from bare to green to gold to bare again.

numbers.did: 他没想到自己过了 thirty years 才知道雪的气味
numbers.quote_anchor: Today, the air smelled like snow, and Mitch couldn’t believe he’d gone thirty years without knowing that scent.

numbers.did: 自 Sydney 走进他生活那天起已 nearly a decade，他一直等着世界崩塌
numbers.quote_anchor: Every day since the girl had walked into his life, nearly a decade before, some part of Mitchell Turner had been waiting for the world—his world—to fall apart.

numbers.did: 她其实离 twenty-first birthday 只差一个月
numbers.quote_anchor: That in truth, she was a month shy of her twenty-first birthday.
